analysis:
All three changed files are test-only. Each change adds handling for a new `.logprobs` case in an exhaustive switch over generation events: FlintResponseFormatTests.swift line 362 (`case .info, .logprobs: break`), QwenJSONAnswerServingTests.swift line 107 (`.toolCall, .toolCallDelta, .logprobs: break`) and NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift line 37 (`case .logprobs: return "L"`). No production source is in this batch, so there is no change to authentication, key handling, attestation, encryption, the coordinator-provider protocol or billing. The tests cover Flint and Qwen response_format constraints, validate that errors never quote generated content (the `PRIVATE` marker check) and map invalid output to HTTP 422 via `ProviderLoop.mapInferenceErrorToStatus`. These test assertions are unchanged by this PR and weaken no existing control.

One integration question remains for the pass that sees production code. A new `.logprobs` event in MLXServerGenerationEvent could expose per-token log probabilities, which are derived from decrypted prompt and completion content (A-001). That pass should check that logprobs are emitted only when the request asks for them. It should also check that they pass through the same hop-by-hop encryption as other response chunks, so a failure never falls back to plaintext (T-008, TB-002), and that logprobs are not leaked to the coordinator logs. That code is not supplied here, and the tests only swallow the event, so I raise no finding. The CBv2 delta in QwenScriptedEngine already carries `logprobs: nil`, which is consistent with logprobs being opt-in. The change does not touch the prefix-cache threat T-041 or the add-on hold socket (TB-012).
